title: The Sword and the Assistant
text: After that, as long as Itsuki kept making excuses, Yuki-chan and the others apparently kept asking him questions. Eventually, the story goes, Itsuki just sat down, covered his ears, and kept his head down. Apparently, they managed to wipe out the monsters that kept appearing and raise Itsuki’s level all the way to 80.
“‘Hey, hey, hey!’”
With that, Yuki-chan and the others resumed questioning Itsuki. Should I join in, too? Itsuki’s friends seem frustrated, but since I’m here, they don’t seem to be able to speak up too strongly.
“Ah, Motoyasu-kun.”
Just then, my Father showed up.
“‘Hey, hey, hey!’”
“W-what are you guys doing?”
As if at a loss for words, my Father addressed Yuki and the others surrounding Itsuki.
“It’s just that Itsuki keeps making excuses, so Yuki-chan and the others are bombarding him with questions.”
“It just looks like they’re bullying him. Shouldn’t you make them stop?”
“Naofumi-san! Please, help us!”
As if a savior had appeared, Itsuki clings to my Father. Oh, it seems Itsuki has finally come to understand Father’s greatness.
“For now… Motoyasu, please convince Yuki and the others to back off from Itsuki.”
“Understood. Alright then, Yuki and the others, please take it easy on the questions for Itsuki and get some rest to prepare for tomorrow.”
“Got it.”
“Yay!”
Yuki and Kou nodded energetically and stepped away from Itsuki.
“Iwa, what about Keel-kun? I’m missing some fluff.”
“Keel-kun’s resting in his room.”
“Got it.”
Luna-chan walks briskly over to Keel. What a heartwarming sight she is from behind.
“Thank you. This is exactly what they mean by ‘a ray of hope in hell.’”
“I have no idea what you’re talking about…”
Then I explained the whole situation to my Father.
“Well, Itsuki has this tendency to keep things secret—or rather… he seems to have such a strong desire to be a hero that trying to hide it probably just made him stand out even more.”
“I wasn’t hiding anything. Yet they surrounded me like I was a criminal and grilled me with questions the whole time. When I tried to run away, they even caught me.”
“I think Yuki-chan and the others have a valid point, don’t you? Even Itsuki wouldn’t want to trust his back to someone who cuts corners in battle, right?”
“Ugh… I wasn’t cutting corners at all.”

“Those kids aren’t human. They’re sensitive in all sorts of ways and can spot a lie over the slightest thing. If they thought you were holding back, wouldn’t it have been better to just say you wanted to see what they were really capable of? Well, that wouldn’t have worked if you actually were holding back, though.”
At Father’s remark, Itsuki glared at him fiercely.
“What? Are you planning to let your emotions get the better of you and cause trouble again? That kind of recklessness won’t fly.”

Even my father is visibly annoyed. There’s no logic to this, after all. Even if Itsuki flies into a rage over Father’s criticism, only his friends would agree with him. Though those friends seem paralyzed whenever I glare at them.
“Anyway, the team swap between Itsuki and Motoyasu is over. I’m sure Itsuki and the others really got a feel for how strong Motoyasu’s group is.”
“……Hmph.”
At Father’s words, Itsuki walks away in silence, looking thoroughly displeased. Itsuki and his friends followed right behind him.
“I hope this helps them understand things a little better.”
“Don’t you think that’s a bit of a stretch?”

Honestly, Itsuki and his friends are a handful. In the future, it seems they were forced to think things through when they couldn’t express themselves due to the Curse Skills’ effects. Itsuki is the type who acts on his emotions.

I’m probably in no position to judge others, but isn’t Itsuki the most confident hero there is? He has a sense of justice that’s stronger than anyone else’s, and you could even say he’s desperate to help others. Itsuki has a very strong desire to be a hero.

He probably doesn’t suspect for a second that the weak might actually be the villains. Well, I never imagined either that someone I trusted would actually be the mastermind behind it all. Because of that, there’s been a rift between me and my Father for quite a long time now.

“That said… in the end, Itsuki’s cooperation is essential if we’re to survive this and save the world. If he does something reckless and dies, it’ll just cause more trouble for Motoyasu-kun, won’t it? And for me… all my hard work up to this point would go down the drain without me even knowing it.”
“That’s true.”

It’s an issue we can’t avoid. After all, the next incident involves the Spirit Tortoise. If we manage to prevent this problem before it happens, what course of action will Itsuki and the others take? Ideally, I’d like them to realize they don’t have time to be fighting among themselves, but judging by Itsuki’s demeanor, there are probably mountains of problems piling up.
“For now, we’ll have to have some discussions so we can coordinate with Ren, Itsuki, and the others.”
“That’s right. By the way, how did things go with your Father?”
My Father shifted his gaze several times when I asked that question.
“Ah… yeah. I didn’t have any major problems on my end. Ren’s group doesn’t cause any trouble and they’re cooperative, after all.”
“Then why did you sound so troubled?”
“Um… it seems the message didn’t get through to Motoyasu and Itsuki, but it looks like a problem came up with Ren’s group. That’s why we called off the hunt this morning and are here now.”
“I see… What happened? By the way, where is Ren?”
“Yeah. Well, a few things happened.”
“Is it a big deal?”
“Well… I guess you could call it a problem. I heard from Sakura-chan and Keel-kun that, actually, Wyndia-chan—”
My father told me about what happened between Ren and his group.
“I’m coming in.”
“It’s open.”

Apparently, Keel stepped forward as the representative of my father-in-law’s group to face off against Ren. Since they’d met a few times before, it seems they were able to welcome Keel and Sakura-chan without any particular issues.
“First things first—let’s introduce ourselves. I’m Ren Amaki, the Sword Hero. I’ll be counting on you for the next two days.”
“We’ve talked before, haven’t we? Sword Guy.”
“…That’s right. You were one of Naofumi’s Demi-Human companions, weren’t you?”
“That’s right. My name’s Keel. And these are Sakura-chan, Wyndia-chan, and Gaelion-chan.”
“Nice to meet you!”
“……Nice to meet you, I guess.”
It seems the assistant and Rival gave Ren a displeased look before greeting him. Ren apparently gave his Father’s companions a sharp, appraising glance.
“I suppose since they’re Naofumi’s companions, there aren’t any humans here, huh?”
“So what?”
“No particular reason.”
“Do we have to be human? Where’s that rule written, I wonder?”
The Assistant reportedly said this in a mocking tone. Ren reportedly glared at the Assistant with a huff, but immediately turned toward Keel.

“It’s not like there aren’t any humans among my brother’s group, but since we’re in charge of combat, we decided to fight alongside Sword-Brother like this. By the way, the humans are Elena-nee and Melty-chan.”
“I see. So, what are your levels?”
It’s said that Ren asked about Keel and the others’ levels in a matter-of-fact tone.
“Huh? Are we leaving already?”
“What level are you?”
“I’m Level 65, Sakura-chan is 67, Wyndia-chan is 63, and Gaelion-chan is 64. As for Big Bro’s aptitude—”
“Naofumi and the others seem to have been fighting more than I thought. If those levels are really accurate, that is.”

It seems Ren interrupted Keel mid-sentence to say that. By the way, it seems my Father lowered their levels slightly by improving their aptitudes before they parted ways, so their hunting efforts wouldn’t go to waste. So their actual levels should be just as high as Yuki-chan’s group. I should’ve just left Yuki-chan’s group as is, too.
“Aren’t you the one with the lower level, actually?”
The assistant says sarcastically, smiling defiantly.
“Hmph, you don’t seem to understand the fundamental difference in strength between a Hero and the people of this world.”
“You’re free to think that.”
“Big sis, you’d better keep quiet for a bit.”
Apparently, the Rival admonished the assistant and put a hand over her mouth. Hmm, so this dragon can read the room, too?
“But… a talking dragon, huh?”
“It’s Gaelion.”
After glancing at the Rival a few times, Ren leaves the room as if he’s lost interest.
“Alright, let’s go hunting. Buy some medicine and whatnot if you need it.”
“I already got some from Naofumi, so I’m all set!”
I got some from my Father, too. Actually, my Father has never once run out of essentials like medicine. This holds true in every world, including the first one.
“I see.”
So, apparently, Ren led them from the harbor to another island.
“Huh? What’s the sword-wielding guy’s level?”
It seems Keel said this to Ren, but it didn’t seem to reach Ren’s ears as he was gazing out at the sea.
